identity.title: The Peculiar Debris Disk of HD 111520 as Resolved by the Gemini Planet Imager

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the Gemini Planet Imager (GPI), we have resolved the circumstellar debris disk around HD 111520 at a projected range of ∼ 30-100 AU in both total and polarized H -band intensity.

evidence.quote: The distance to the system was measured to be 108 ± 12 pc (van Leeuwen 2007), which we adopt throughout this study.

question.value: What is the near-IR scattered-light morphology, brightness asymmetry and polarization of the HD 111520 debris disk, with archival far-IR/mm photometry (incl. ALMA) used for SED context?

evidence.quote: We therefore present GPI data which resolves the disk inside 1 ″ to better probe the structure of the disk.

method.value: Archived ALMA continuum maps measured with a 2.5 arcsec aperture; RMS from random apertures of same size

evidence.quote: ALMA continuum maps were retrieved from the ALMA Science Archive and was measured with an 2 ″. 5 aperture.

method.value: Kurucz stellar model plus two modified blackbodies, least-squares weighted by photometric uncertainties

evidence.quote: The star subtracted flux densities were then least-squares fit with two modified blackbody SEDs using the photometric uncertainties as weights.

key_parameters.value: Kurucz Teff 6750 K; knee 173 µm, beta 0.8

evidence.quote: The modified slope parameters include a knee at 173 µm with a β index of 0.8

assumptions.value: Blackbody dust temperatures, stellar luminosity 2.9 Lsun for radii

evidence.quote: Given a stellar luminosity 2.9 L ⊙ and assuming blackbody temperatures for the dust

fitting.value: Least squares; uncertainties from diagonal of covariance matrix

evidence.quote: Uncertainties were determined using the diagonal of the covariance matrix
The spectral mode cubes were combined with pyKLIP (Wang et al. 2015) using ADI-only mode

claims.hypothesis: What is the disk asymmetry and its cause?
claims.experiment: GPI imaging with three PSF subtraction methods
claims.result: 2:1 NW/SE brightness asymmetry; polarization fraction similar on both sides
claims.finding: Azimuthal dust density variation likely causes the asymmetry

evidence.quote: The combination of large brightness asymmetry and symmetric polarization fraction leads us to believe that an azimuthal dust density variation is causing the observed asymmetry.

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties do not include systematic biases such as non-blackbody grains; knee and beta uncertain

evidence.quote: given the lack of photometric coverage near the knee, both parameters remain uncertain

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA used only as one photometric point from an unresolved source
